**404-26** 

Minutes of September 15, 2026 to be approved.

A motion was made by Councillor Taylor, seconded by Councillor Condon, that the Committee Minutes of September 15, 2026 be approved. The motion carried by a unanimous vote.

## Business

**363-26** 

Mayoral Appointment: Karen Buck of 323 Forest Street, Malden, as member of the Public Works Commission, said term to commence upon confirmation by the City Council and expire on March 1, 2027.

Sponsors: Peg Crowe

Attachments: Mayor's Appointment Letter - Karen Buck

Councillor Crowe welcomed Karen Buck, Mayoral Appointment as a member of the Public Works Commission and explained she likes to have a conversational approach for the meeting and asked Karen to tell the committee about herself and what spoke to her to about this Board or Commission.

Karen explained that they were invited to join the Public Works Commission and had a great conversation with Diego Barricelli, Chair of DPW Commission. They discussed the commission’s role in addressing water-bill concerns, including leaks, fairness in assistance decisions, curb-cut reviews, and public education about water conservation. They also described their connection to the Department of Public Works and interest in maintaining the storm water system.

Councillor Taylor said she is excited to see Karen here and thanks her for wanting to give even more back to the community by serving on this commission. She asked what is the one thing she is excited about and strength that she has that will be useful here.

Karen said community and she identified long-standing community connections through work involving the Malden River and described a goal of strengthening communication and education between the Department of Public Works and residents.

Councillor McDonald said you have done so much work on the recurrent and environmental sustainability of the City, the Public Works Commission, overseeing the tree canopy, working with the tree board and the sewer system and runoff system. What are your thoughts about how the Public Works Commission can be a really strong partner in our climate action plan and goals in preparing the city for rising temperatures?

Karen said the tree canopy is very important to me. She described a tree stewardship program developed with Chris Rosa, Cemetery Director & Tree Warden, including two workshops and approximately 30 residents prepared to identify tree issues and also highlighted drought-related risks to Malden’s tree canopy and the need for residents to water and care for street and privately owned trees. She also discussed adopting storm drains through a partnership with the Mystic River Watershed Association, maintaining storm water infrastructure at the city yard, and considering rain gardens and trenches that divert storm water toward trees. In response to a question about expanding permeable pavement, they said it is costly and may not always last, while describing storm water-diversion features as potentially useful complementary approaches.

Councillor O'Malley asked Karen why the Public Works Commission and not the Conservation Commission and explained that we do not have many people who volunteer for boards and commissions and so part of our thing is also figuring out are people being fitted into the right slots and maybe that's the case. I just would like to hear why.

Karen said I am not an engineer by any means. She enjoys the Department of Public Works and works well with Chris Rosa and the staff.

Councillor Crowe said I appreciate you coming forward and look forward it is interesting as you said, Public Works Commission to solve the things that you can talk about kind of holds a lot of things together and certainly for you.

A motion was made by Councillor Taylor, seconded by Councillor Condon, that the Appointment be recommended favorably to the City Council. The motion carried by the following vote:

Yea: 4 - Councillor Crowe, Councillor Taylor, Councillor Colon Hayes and Councillor Condon

**364-26** 

Mayoral Appointment: Heather Barry of 10 Hudson Terrace, Malden, as member of the Parks and Recreation Commission, said term to commence upon confirmation by the City Council and expire on June 30, 2028.

Sponsors: Peg Crowe

Attachments: Mayor's Appointment Letter - Heather Barry

Councillor Crowe said she was aware that there was a question when the appointments were getting referred about two people who are also City Employees being on this board. This is not a stipend commission and they are very qualified to be on this commission. It is nice to have members with their expertise. She begins with Heather and asks her to tell the committee a little about herself and what you think about the parks and recreation commission.

Heather has been a Malden resident since 2001. She feels her son has played in every park and has birthday parties so a lot of use of the parks. She's been involved with the Malden Community Garden, Malden reads, and Malden CPAC over at the schools. She is currently the President of Malden Soccer and has worked a lot with Joe Levine, Rec Director over the years and done a lot of like photography and other things for them.

She has also done a lot with football as well. When the announcement came out about the new Commission, it seemed like she had been looking for a way to kind of contribute to government and some of the things, like Public Works. didn't necessarily was up her alley. Here she feels like she could contribute in a range of ways, She explained her interest in thinking through both how the parks are used, how they're accessible, how they're safe and how to rebalance the different usages and help people know where the parks are and how to use them. What she would like to avoid but is very peripherally involved, is all the controversy over the Salemwood Park and what would happen whether grass or turf, and felt like the way that devolved into such a terrible interaction she would not have that happen over anything that we do going forward. She works in Medford at Tufts University and a lot of the work is global, but also a lot of the work is around conflict and difficult conversations and things like that so that's kind of what drew her. She knows it's a new Commission, and doesn't know if it has a charge yet, aside from something that the committee has to work on.

The Pers/Appts Committee asked the following questions with all the candidates. However each vote was taken individually and is reflected in the minutes for the record.

Councillor Taylor made a statement that she really thinks it's great when starting off this Commission that we have such a like different backgrounds coming together to really build on what's going on at the rec department. That's going to be important when we're looking at permitting and what the fields are being used for and what uses you see come in and requests for accessibility and what you bring to the table. Then just where a new resident coming in and seeing what she has seen and a small child versus older kids is a great way to start to build on this. Again she appreciates those of you who work for the city and that are willing to come without a second thought and be here to put this time in and also thanks them for sharing their talents with us.

Councillor McDonald explained that Parks and Recreation had historically been absorbed under Public Works and that the separate commission should clarify responsibility and decision-making for city parks and emphasized the need for a parks and recreation plan establishing priorities for accessibility, equity, availability, maintenance, and long-term stewardship. Councillor McDonald raised concerns about users occupying parks disproportionately, including a specific concern involving a regional charter school and asked the Members of the Commission if they are prepared for the hard permitting conversations about people using the parks under the alignment with the law?

Julie Turner answered absolutely it is in her daily work load.

Councillor O'Malley looked at one of the major responsibilities of this commission and they maintain the parks and asked what is something they would like to see to improve managing our Parks?

Heather identified fast-moving scooters, motorized bicycles, and similar vehicles as a safety and field-maintenance concern and suggested considering designated areas or other methods to keep these vehicles away from children and active recreation areas.

Ben discussed the challenge of maintaining landscaping and facilities after major projects are completed and emphasized that maintenance plans are needed so that large investments in parks and public spaces remain functional and attractive over time, including projects with extensive plantings.

Jane noted that residents frequently ask about dedicating benches or other park features, but the city lacks a clearly established process. The commission was expected to consider formal procedures for dedications and for newer park uses that do not fit existing permit categories.

Julie added there are different categories to dedicating benches or other park features and the commission will help with specific permitting and pricing and establishing the process.

A motion was made by Councillor Taylor, seconded by Councillor Colon Hayes, that the Appointment be recommended favorably to the City Council. The motion carried by the following vote:

Yea: 4 - Councillor Crowe, Councillor Taylor, Councillor Colon Hayes and Councillor Condon

**365-26** 

Mayoral Appointment: Ben Gately of 69 Pierce Street, Unit 1, Malden, as member of the Parks and Recreation Commission, said term to commence upon confirmation by the City Council and expire on June 30, 2029.

Sponsors: Peg Crowe

Attachments: Mayor's Appointment Letter - Ben Gately

Ben Gately said he is relatively new two year resident of Malden. He previously worked with the city as a Housing Program Coordinator in OSPCD. He explained in that role, he went through all the hands on with all the Malden residents experiencing housing difficulties, working to create more housing opportunities with any of the city. But also like learning from my colleagues and hearing from residents and like even being as a resident, it's glaring that there's so much opportunity to wait in the city for growth especially with the implementation of the common action plan. There's so much untapped potential, and as a newer resident newer generation getting involved in local politics, I seize the opportunity as serious as I saw this posting, I was incredibly excited to throw my hat in the ring. He was happy to get invited on to be before you all today but with the parks and recreation , he considers himself a frequent visitor.

A motion was made by Councillor Taylor, seconded by Councillor Colon Hayes, that the Appointment be recommended favorably to the City Council. The motion carried by the following vote:

Yea: 4 - Councillor Crowe, Councillor Taylor, Councillor Colon Hayes and Councillor Condon

**367-26** 

Mayoral Appointment: Julie Turner of 265 Forest Street, Malden, as member of the Parks and Recreation Commission, said term to commence upon confirmation by the City Council and expire on June 30, 2028.

Sponsors: Peg Crowe

Attachments: Mayor's Appointment Letter - Julie Turner

Letter regarding P&R Appointments 090826

Julie Turner, Recreation Clerk and is already there and already issuing the permits kind of based on their old system, really looking forward to a new system and trying to accommodate more than just sports permits. We've been working a lot on rock climbing on Waitts Mount and things like getting a better system that builds muscles. She has been a resident of Malden her whole life and has raised her children here. She has been in the parks everyday of her entire life if not multiple fields and she sees some of the things that need to be repaired and also things that work and she looks forward to being on this commission.

A motion was made by Councillor Taylor, seconded by Councillor Colon Hayes, that the Appointment be recommended favorably to the City Council. The motion carried by the following vote:

Yea: 4 - Councillor Crowe, Councillor Taylor, Councillor Colon Hayes and Councillor Condon

**368-26** 

Mayoral Appointment: Jane Ventrone of 33 Dodge Street, Malden, as member of the Parks and Recreation Commission, said term to commence upon confirmation by the City Council and expire on June 30, 2029.

Sponsors: Peg Crowe

Attachments: Mayor's Appointment Letter - Jane Ventrone

Letter regarding P&R Appointments 090826

Jane Ventrone said she is the Director of Housing and Development for the City of Malden. She has been a Malden resident since 2018. As part of her job she does a lot of work within our parks. She explains she is sure everyone here knows we've been spending lots of money, mostly federal money, on upgrading lots of our parks and she loves doing that. She has been learning a lot about the various parks and funding with a wide variety of people in the city, DPW, Chris Rosa, Cemetery Director, Joe Levine, Rec Director and all these new people on the commission. She explained she didn't think much before about how many people it takes to maintain and have these parks run and work well and make them beautiful and feels this is an opportunity to connect all of us in an official way to get all of these people to work together. She mentions also just thinking about the really large dollar investments that we're putting into the parks and making sure that more as you think about maintenance and sort of making sure those dollars are lasting far into the future and keeping parks and really in good shape. She also has a daughter who is 4 and they are major park users.

A motion was made by Councillor Taylor, seconded by Councillor Colon Hayes, that the Appointment be recommended favorably to the City Council. The motion carried by the following vote:

Yea: 4 - Councillor Crowe, Councillor Taylor, Councillor Colon Hayes and Councillor Condon

## Other Business

## Adjournment

Yea: 4 - Councillor Crowe, Councillor Taylor, Councillor Colon Hayes and Councillor Condon
